title: Is the learned rise in attacks carried by the movement neurons' input weights?
question: In AB and AC, learning among social peers barely paid and raised the attack rate, with or without the frustration drive. An exploratory probe after AC (tools/probes/frozen_rows_probe.py) froze the input weights of one group of actions during learning. Freezing the social actions' inputs raised attacks further; freezing the movement actions' inputs removed the rise and gave the largest gain. This study tests that on new seeds.
background: Same design as AC's social12: fixed dynamics (substeps=32, reset_each_decision, normalize with normalize_to='innate'), 12 social agents, 24 food, no hazards, frustration drive on, all agents train together for 1500 ticks, agent 0 tested frozen among frozen peers on 8 held-out worlds against a fresh untrained group. frozen_inputs lists actions whose input weights never learn (they are still renormalised, which leaves frozen rows unchanged). Probe on spent seeds 870-875, 4 test worlds 9800-9803: learning gain +3.8 / -2.4 / +5.6 and trained attack rate 0.196 / 0.291 / 0.022 (untrained 0.050) for learn_all / freeze_social / freeze_moves. Interpretation rule, fixed in advance: learning in the movement neurons carries the rise in attacks if H51a and H51b are supported. H51c and H51d ask whether freezing movement inputs restores a learning gain. Seeds 3200-3211 and worlds 9920-9927 have never been run.

hypotheses.statement: When only the movement inputs learn, learning raises the attack rate
Freezing the movement inputs shrinks the rise in attack rate that learning causes
With the movement inputs frozen, learning pays among social peers
Freezing the movement inputs raises the learning gain
